opening: We want to put a complex structure on the six-sphere S^6.
phrasing: Do not start with the sphere. Start with a family of complex two-tori: a shape that can change while remaining locally understandable.
The base has three special places: one with order 3, one with order 4, and the cusp at infinity.
At the cusp, the torus does not simply disappear. Its cycles twist: this is monodromy.
The twisted fibre degenerates into a six-sided toric surface, the degree-six del Pezzo surface dP6.
The translations used to glue the pieces make the fundamental group trivial: the space has no remaining loop obstruction.
Its integral homology is that of S^6. The construction closes the family into a complex threefold diffeomorphic to S^6.
The answer is yes; the film has shown where the yes comes from.
camera_contract: show closure after the obstruction disappears
